name: Johann IV. von Dražice
summary:
Johann IV of Dražice (1250-1343) was the penultimate Bishop of Prague, serving from 1301 to 1343. His successor, Arnošt of Pardubice, became the first Archbishop of Prague in 1343. Johann IV played a significant role in bringing the Luxembourg dynasty to the Bohemian throne and was a notable patron of architecture and the arts.

As Bishop of Prague, Johann IV oversaw extensive building projects, including the reconstruction of St. Vitus Cathedral and the construction of new chapels and monasteries. He also supported the establishment of new trade routes and fostered cultural exchange with neighboring regions.

Johann IV's influence extended beyond his ecclesiastical duties, as he played a key role in the politics of the Holy Roman Empire. His relationships with powerful nobles and monarchs helped secure the Luxembourg dynasty's claim to the Bohemian throne.

The legacy of Johann IV of Dražice can be seen in the many architectural and cultural achievements that he facilitated during his tenure as Bishop of Prague. His efforts helped shape the city's landscape and contributed to the development of a unique regional identity.

Like many historical figures, Johann IV's life was marked by both personal triumphs and tragic losses. Despite his significant contributions to the church and politics of his time, he ultimately died in 1343 at the age of 93.
